articles.title: Where does Utah rank in some of Morgan Scalley’s key stats for success?
articles.summary: With Utah sitting atop the Big 12 Conference at 7-0, let’s take a look at where the Utes rank in some of Morgan Scalley’s key stats.
articles.body:
Each week, Utah coach Morgan Scalley and his staff pore over film to prepare the team for the opposing team's tendencies and to try to find any weaknesses that the Utes can exploit.

While watching Houston's film, Utah noticed that Houston allowed a lot of quarterback running lanes. Quarterback Devon Dampier was able to use that to his advantage, rushing for 150 yards and two touchdowns in the Utes' 21-13 win over the Cougars.

"We always take what the defense gives us," Dampier said. "Just watching film, there was a lot of running lanes, quarterback lanes during dropback passes. (Coaches) just emphasized, 'Devon, if you see it, go take it.'"

The eye test and film breakdowns are king in football, but statistics and analytics have their place as well, especially as predictors of future success.

Scalley has studied the best teams in college football over the past 20 years and has identified statistics that are indicative of success.

Obviously, scoring offense and defense are the two most important statistics, but digging deeper, what are others that lead to wins?

Rush defense, Scalley says, is a big one. While total rushing yards "doesn't show up as a big stat" for the current top teams in the country, yards per rush is a big tell.

"Are you rushing the ball efficiently? Same thing, passing the ball. Are you passing the ball efficiently? Passing yards, that will never show up. I mean, it rarely shows up in your top programs," Scalley said.

Other telling stats that Scalley looks at include turnover margin and punt return yards.

In his studies, a good amount of the stats most predictive to team success over the past 20 years are on the defensive side of the ball.

"It's why playing great defense is so huge and protecting the football. Chunk yardage plays shows up quite a bit," Scalley said.

With Utah sitting atop the Big 12 Conference at 7-0 and one of just three undefeated teams left in college football, let's take a look at where the Utes rank in some of the stats Scalley mentioned.

Scoring offense: 37.4 points per game (No. 14 in the nation)

The Utes' offense has been potent, especially to start the season. Utah ranks No. 2 in the Big 12 in points per game, but when filtering to just conference games, that number dips from 37.4 points to 30 points, which ranks fifth in the 16-team Big 12.

After scoring at least 31 points in their first five games, Utah has seen a bit of a dip in the last two, scoring 27 points in a win over Colorado and 21 in the victory against Houston.

Scoring defense: 14.6 points per game (No. 9)

Despite allowing more passing yards — 224.1, No. 91 in the nation — than we've come to expect from a typical Utah defense, it hasn't impacted the number that actually matters — opposing points per game.

Utah's defense ranks as one of the best in the country, holding opponents to just 14.6 points per game. In conference play, Utah is allowing 19.5, but still hasn't allowed more than 24 points in any Big 12 game this season.

The standout defensive performance by the Utes came last weekend as Utah held Houston to just 13 points — 26 points below their season average.

The biggest reason why the Utes have kept their opponents' scores low has been a stingy red zone defense. Opponents are scoring in the red zone just 70.6% of the time, 10th-best in the nation, and scoring touchdowns just 47% of the time inside the 20-yard line.

Yards per rush: 5.65 (No. 10); Yards per rush allowed: 3.2 (No. 22)

When Utah runs the ball, it is getting 5.65 yards per rush, good for No. 10 in the nation. Only Big 12 foes Cincinnati — the Utes' next opponent — and Kansas State are averaging more yards per rush.

Wayshawn Parker has been one of the best running backs in the nation and is averaging 6.3 yards per carry, even though teams have keyed in on him as of late. Dampier also contributes to that statistic with 4.7 yards per rush, an impressive showing considering sacks count against quarterback rushing yards in college football.

The Utes have faced some good rushing attacks, like Houston, and have largely shut them down. Utah has been one of the best teams against the rush and have made teams one-dimensional.

Passing efficiency: 158.09 (No. 25); Defensive pass efficiency: 104.24 (No. 6)

The NCAA uses this formula to calculate team passing efficiency, per sports-reference.com : 8.4 * Yds + 330 * TD - 200 * Int + 100 * Cmp) / Att.

Utah, led by Dampier, is No. 25 in the country with a passing efficiency rating of 158.09. That rating is despite six interceptions thrown by Dampier, tied for the most of any team ranked in the top 25 in passing efficiency.

Meanwhile, the defense has been effective in forcing incompletions and holding opposing quarterbacks well below their average completion percentage.

Utah has thrown six interceptions and lost two fumbles, but still has a plus-three turnover margin on the year. The Utes have lived up to the "ballhawks" in Scalley's RSNB initialism, snagging eight interceptions and recovering three fumbles, including a huge one last week that was forced by a Jackson Bennee sack and recovered by Jireh Moe.

Scalley did caution that Dampier has to cut down the interceptions.

"We can't turn the ball over. There's them taking the ball away and then there's us turning it over just with bad decision making and we've had a couple of those," Scalley said.

Punt return yards: 6.67 per return (No. 99); Opposing punt return yards: -0.25 (No. 2)

Utah punt returner Mana Carvalho, who returned a punt for a touchdown last year against Cincinnati, hasn't broken a big one yet, and has had a couple of close calls fielding the ball.

The Utes are averaging just 6.67 yards per punt return, which ranks near the bottom of the FBS.

On the flip side, Utah is No. 2 in the country in punt return defense, holding opponents to -0.25 yards per punt return. Opposing teams haven't had many chances to return the ball, either, with just four returns on the season.

Chunk plays: 77 (No. 8); Opposing chunk plays: 40 (No. 20)

Defining chunk plays as passes of 20 or more yards and runs of 10 or more yards, Utah is tied for No. 8 in the country with 77. The Utes have 51 rushes of 10 or more yards and 26 passes of 20 or more yards.

On defense, Utah is limiting long rushing plays (there have been just 19 rushes of 10 or more yards against the Utes), but have allowed 21 passes of 20 or more yards.

articles.title: Carter Hart injury update: Golden Knights goalie out after leaving morning skate
articles.summary: Vegas' Carter Hart suffered what seemed to be a lower body injury during the morning skate. He was later ruled out for Oct. 27's game.
articles.body:
Vegas Golden Knights goalie Carter Hart was ruled out for Oct. 27's game against the Ottawa Senators , with the goalie exiting during the morning skate on Tuesday.

Hart, who seemingly suffered a lower body injury, appeared to have a limp, per The Hockey News' Hannah Kirkell.

Vegas coach Ryan Craig confirmed Hart would miss the Golden Knights' home game and Adin Hill would start in his place. Hart has a 2.76 goals against average in this fledgling season and an .889 save percentage.

Craig would not provide further updates.

Hart exited the morning skate on Oct. 27 with what appeared to be a lower body injury, as he moved with a noticeable limp.

It is unknown what the extent of Hart's injury is.

Hill has played five games this season, posting a 2.96 goals against average and a save percentage of .882.

The Golden Knights are 4-1 in his starts.

articles.title: Spurs bring designer streetwear, cowboy flair to Frost Bank Center ahead of Kings game
articles.summary: Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper, Devin Vassell and Keldon Johnson showed off their game-day fashion ahead of Tuesday's matchup against the Sacramento Kings.
articles.body:
The San Antonio Spurs brought a mix of luxury streetwear, bold graphics and Texas cowboy flair to Frost Bank Center on Tuesday ahead of their matchup against the Sacramento Kings.

Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper, Devin Vassell and Keldon Johnson showed off their personal styles as they arrived at the arena. Designer labels including Balenciaga, Chrome Hearts, Carhartt WIP and ERCOLE STUDIO made appearances.

The Slash Bros arrived together, with the young Spurs teammates sporting contrasting streetwear looks.

Castle made a statement in a bright red Balenciaga hoodie featuring the fashion house's logo across the chest. He paired it with Balenciaga VIC Skater Graffiti sweatpants, which had an oversized fit and black-and-white, graffiti-inspired graphics. He completed the look with a black-and-white Chrome Hearts Skully Cross Logo beanie and a black backpack.

Harper kept things simple alongside Castle, wearing a black Nike Kobe Bryant hoodie with a small gold Mamba logo on the chest. The Spurs rookie completed his laid-back look with black pants and white sneakers.

Vassell opted for a graphic-heavy streetwear look, wearing an ERCOLE STUDIO gray graphic-print raw-edge T-shirt. The blue-gray shirt featured a woman's face and a lighthouse, with "Holy Water" printed across the front. He paired it with loose-fitting black pants and gray sneakers and carried blue over-ear headphones.

Johnson, meanwhile, brought a little Texas swagger to the arena in a black cowboy hat and a red, black and white Carhartt WIP plaid patch-pocket shirt layered over a black T-shirt. He paired the Western-inspired outfit with black pants and a silver cross necklace. His mustache added another touch of cowboy flair.

From Castle and Harper's coordinated arrival to Johnson's Western-inspired outfit, the Spurs continued to showcase their individual personalities through their game-day fashion.

San Antonio hosts Sacramento on Tuesday night at Frost Bank Center. Tipoff is scheduled for 7 p.m.

articles.title: Hellebuyck Returns Ready To Play For New Jersey Against Dallas
articles.summary: Connor Hellebuyck skips the waiting game, declaring himself ready for Tuesday's debut with New Jersey despite a long suspension and trade standoff.
articles.body:
Connor Hellebuyck is not waiting for permission to start playing again. The veteran goaltender told reporters on Monday that he feels ready to go right now, even though he has not played a game this season. His first appearance in New Jersey comes Tuesday night versus the Dallas Stars, occurring merely four days after a trade from Winnipeg concluded a months-long standoff.

Many athletes let their skills fade when they are stuck on the sidelines, but Hellebuyck did not take that route. ESPN reports that he practiced five to six days weekly in Michigan while suspended. Robby Fabbri and Antonio Stranges, both free agent forwards, trained with him, and he approached these sessions with the same intensity as a full NHL camp. He noted that the goalposts were not drilled into the ice like they are for real games, and both forwards shot left-handed, which limited his practice options. Yet he kept working. He said, "If you're asking me, I'm ready today," Hellebuyck said Monday. "But I don't make every decision around here."

The trade that brought him to New Jersey cost the Devils a significant package. The team sent forward Dawson Mercer, goaltender Nico Daws, prospect Alexander Command, and two draft picks to Winnipeg. This move marks the biggest play yet for first-year general manager Sunny Mehta. Mehta was hired this summer after working with the Florida Panthers. The Devils currently sit at 7-4-0 and are riding a three-game win streak into this road trip.

After spending 11 years with the Winnipeg Jets, Hellebuyck knows the league well, but he still has work to do on his timing. Winnipeg signed him in 2023 to a seven-year contract, and he is currently in the third year of that deal. During that time, he forfeited more than $900,000 in salary because he did not report to training camp. Now he must relearn how to handle screens and rebounds in a new system. "The important part is seeing some screens and reacting to some rebounds, and getting a feel for some righties," said Hellebuyck.

His last start came on April 13 against the Vegas Golden Knights, where he allowed six goals on 38 shots. The Dallas Stars head into Tuesday after winning their last five games. Hellebuyck has a mixed history against Dallas, holding a 14-12-6 record in 32 career meetings. However, his last seven matchups with the Stars have been rough, with just one win and a 3.20 goals-against average. Despite these stats, the mood is positive. "I'm just really excited to play hockey again," Hellebuyck said. "That was the hardest part about all of this, wanting to go back and not being able to."

New Jersey has only one other goalie on the roster, veteran Jake Allen. This means Hellebuyck's arrival immediately changes the team's dynamic. The three-time Vezina Trophy winner and Olympic gold medalist brings a proven track record to a young squad. He finished his tenure with the Jets with a 345-208-55 record over 625 games. That franchise's record in nearly every major goaltending category, such as wins and shutouts, is led by him. The team now faces a tough test against a red-hot Dallas club that looks to extend their winning streak to six games.

articles.title: 49ers star ‘tracking well’ to return after bye week
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers GM John Lynch likes one of his star's chances to return after the bye week.
articles.body:
Nick Bosa's long wait to return appears to be nearing its end.

49ers general manager John Lynch said Tuesday on KNBR that the star edge rusher is "tracking well" to be back after San Francisco's bye week. Bosa has missed the last five games, dating to Week 3, with a calf injury.

Lynch explained how the team landed on holding him out through the bye despite hope he could return as early as Week 6, and added that that decision wasn't because of an injury setback.

"Bosa had a calf strain, and those are tough. It's another one where you don't want any tightness and soreness, because a reinjury keeps you out even longer," Lynch said. "Kyle was very forthright. Nick was feeling very good. He had pushed it the week prior to the Commanders game and was feeling really good. Then he went out, took it to the next level of where he was actually doing D-line drills, and he got a little sore, and I think that gave everyone pause. That's a signal that it's too soon. I don't think it was a setback. It was just a reality that he wasn't quite there at that point.

The decision was made: let's get him through the bye week. He's got to go through the week of practice, but he's tracking well to be back. Now the goal is to have him back and keep him back, because he's a difference-maker when he's on the field."

Bosa's return is still not locked in, though. He still has to get through a full week of practice, and Lynch's emphasis on keeping him back suggests the 49ers will be careful with a player who got sore the last time he ramped up.

The timing matters for a team that is 6-1 despite the injuries, but fell 29-20 to the Falcons on Sunday. The 49ers return from the bye against the Raiders, and the defensive line would get a major boost if Bosa is back for that game.

articles.title: Did Deion Sanders really offer critics $50,000 to shut up? Here’s the real story
articles.summary: Would Colorado football coach Deion Sanders really pay $50,000 to critics to stop taking about him? No, but he had a point.
articles.body:
Colorado football coach Deion Sanders spent a portion of his weekly news conference Oct. 27 debunking a claim he offered $50,000 to certain people to keep them quiet and stop criticizing him .

"That was a joke," Sanders said Tuesday.

But the claim still caught fire on the internet nonetheless, benefiting from the combustible atmosphere of Sanders' struggles in 2026. His team is 2-5 after five consecutive losses , leading to heightened criticism of Sanders as his team prepares to face Kansas State at home Oct. 31. It marked the latest flash point in a simmering drama between supporters of Sanders and Colorado football fans that have gotten fed up with losing.

Here's how it started and how it's going.

The claim stems from a point Sanders made earlier this year that if he offered some people $25,000 or $50,000 to stop talking, writing and criticizing him and his family for a year, they wouldn't take it because they'd lose money.

"Let's see how that works" Sanders said on Thee Pregame Show in May .

He didn't frame it as a serious offer. He was making a point. There are content creators and news media dedicated to covering what he says and trying to stir the pot about him.

How did this false claim catch fire recently?

One of Sanders' friends, Christopher Neely, came with Sanders from Jackson State to Colorado, where Neely does a podcast on the team and is known as loyal supporter of Sanders. He is granted access to Sanders and his program in exchange.

As criticism about Sanders shot up after a 57-24 loss at Oklahoma State on Oct. 24, Neely recalled Sanders' previous point about the $50,000. He talked about it during a podcast last weekend .

"The people that attack you wouldn't be making the money they were making if he wasn't here (in Colorado) to attack," Neely said. "Which is why he told some of them, 'Hey man, just let's just do this. I give you $50,000 to not mention my name for a year.' And ain't nobody took the deal yet."

Social media users and bloggers took this literally and ran with it without getting further verification under old journalism standards. But he was referring to Sanders' previous point. Then a reporter asked Sanders about it at his weekly news conference on Tuesday.

What Deion Sanders said about $50,000 'offer' Tuesday

A reporter asked him, "Have you offered money for people not to criticize you?"

Neely, who sits near Sanders at news conferences, then reminded Sanders what he said in May — about how some wouldn't take a hypothetical offer of $50,000 to not talk about it for a year because it would be bad for their business.

"Oh, no, no, no," Sanders said told the reporter who asked him about the money offer. "I think you misinterpreted that."

"I would never offer a man money," Sanders said. "I don't give a damn what you say about me. That was really a joke about someone prospering off of your name and your brand, but they don't like you."

Follow reporter Brent Schrotenboer @Schrotenboer . Email: bschrotenb@usatoday.com

articles.title: 3 things that stood out from Purdue basketball's blowout exhibition loss at UConn
articles.summary: The Boilermakers did not shoot it well, and it led to playing from behind. Here's what we learned in the preseason finale.
articles.body:
HARTFORD, CT — Purdue basketball received the challenge it wanted from UConn in its final exhibition and then some, falling 76-53 at PeoplesBank Arena on Tuesday.

The Boilermakers remained winless in their recent run of exhibition road games against high-major opponents. C.J. Cox scored 18 points, but functional offense was hard to come by for much of the night.

Purdue basketball photos vs. UConn in college basketball action

Purdue couldn't make a 3, couldn't muster enough functional offense elsewhere

Matt Painter wanted to play UConn for the simple reason the Huskies "run good offense and make it hard for you to run good offense." He probably wasn't expecting a 1-for-14 first-half shooting performance from 3, a handful of missed opportunities inside and a generally flat offensive performance. (That one made 3 came when Raleigh Burgess whiffed a layup but got the ball back and found Jack Benter behind the line.)

Purdue does not need to be explosive on offense this season, but it must be efficient. Instead, it looked off-kilter for much of the first half. Between those missed 3s and turnovers it had 18 empty offensive possessions in the first half alone. It finished 2_-25 from 3, which probably won't happen often. The inability to create fast break chances or finish around the rim may actually be bigger concerns.

Purdue received a final rebounding reminder before season's start

UConn projected as a much more significant rebounding challenge, and delivered. Three of the Huskies' offensive rebounds came on one possession which did not yield points, but in general, Purdue had a harder time rewarding itself for stops than in the first two exhibitions. UConn also set a tone with the way it attacked off defensive rebounds, beating the Boilers down the floor for a couple of 3s and a run-out dunk in the first eight minutes of the game.

When Purdue flipped the rebounding advantage in the opening minutes of the second half, it started to cut into the lead. It simply couldn't convert enough on offense to ever challenge to take the lead.

Braylon Mullins back on the floor, again facing off with Luke Ertel

Greenfield-Central alum Braylon Mullins made his exhibition debut for UConn after missing the first two with an unspecified injury. He provided some hints as to his affliction, though, wearing braces on both knees. When he subbed out of the game, he immediately went to a stationary bike positioned near the court. Purdue kept the NCAA Tournament hero in check — seven points on 3-9 shooting — but he also distributed four assists in the first half.

He and Purdue freshman Luke Ertel, a Mt. Vernon grad, went head-to-head in some memorable high school games. He scored two points on 1-4 shooting in this Hancock County reunion.

Nathan Baird and Sam King have the best Purdue sports coverage, and sign up for IndyStar's Boilermakers newsletter .
